summary: Granite tower in Lake Superior, 12.5 statute miles north of Marquette: lit 1869, keepers to 1937, now private and closed; a 1995 Coast Guard light stands beside it.

structures.note: 40 ft (12 m) per Rowlett and LighthouseFriends; USLHS gives 34 ft (10.4 m) to the lantern centre

access.note: Private island reached only by boat. Grounds, dwelling and tower closed (LighthouseFriends); site open, tower closed (Rowlett).

events.note: Tower and keeper's house built of granite; materials landed after the 1868 navigation season opened

Oil vapour changed to acetylene; characteristic a white flash every 15 s
Rowlett: inactive since 1939. Disputed: LighthouseFriends describes the signal in 1943.
White flash every 5 s; carbon-dioxide fog bell discontinued
NPGallery publication date 4 August 1983; LighthouseFriends gives 1969
Coast Guard steel skeletal light near the historic tower (USCG 7-14700); Rowlett lists it as active
Sold by sealed bid on 19 October 1999 to a private buyer
First keeper Isaac P. Bridges drowned on his way home from Garlic Point
Keeper of the Marquette light, son of the Granite Island keeper, drowned; the Marquette station keeper fetched the father by steam launch
Assistant keeper John McMartin drowned after a boat was dashed against the rocks

corrections.why: The record's 15.0 m matches neither Rowlett and LighthouseFriends (40 ft, 12 m) nor the USLHS place record (34 ft, 10.4 m). 12.2 m follows the two sources that agree; the USLHS figure is kept in notes.

corrections.current: Fl W 6s, focal height 29.3 m, range 9.5 nmi (attached to the 1869 station)
corrections.proposed: Those values describe the 1995 Coast Guard steel tower (USCG 7-14700), which Rowlett lists as active with a white flash every 6 s and a focal plane of 96 ft (29 m). The 1869 tower is recorded as inactive.
corrections.why: Rowlett's 1995 tower entry matches the record's focal height and characteristic. The historic station's record should not carry the modern light's characteristic.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The sources answer different questions. The 1869 tower has been inactive since 1939 (Rowlett) and the USLHS record says it is not an active aid, with its optic removed. A separate Coast Guard skeletal tower built in 1995 stands close by and is active (Rowlett). The record's light data match that tower.
The story gives both: the NPGallery asset record gives publication 8/4/1983, and LighthouseFriends says 1969.

notes_for_editor: Roster matched to the USLHS place by name and position (0.31 km) and printed verbatim; the roster comes from the NARA registers via Kraig Anderson's inventory, so a name used beyond this story should be confirmed in a primary register. The NRHP nomination PDF (83000884) is a not-digitised placeholder; the 1983 listing comes from the NPGallery asset record. The Light-House Board reports for 1868, 1869, 1870 and 1879 are not in the local corpus (its Board volumes cover 1891-1901). Their wording is cited through graniteisland.com's transcriptions, a secondary source; check the originals before quoting them in print. The 1891 and 1899 Board volumes and the 1898 Life-Saving Service record are checked against the corpus scans. The 1898 record does not name the keepers; the link of Granite's keeper to the Marquette keeper (son) is from LighthouseFriends and the roster. Sources disagree on how William H. Wheatley drowned on 30 April 1898: LighthouseFriends says his boat capsized in a squall while fishing; the owners' page says he drowned in a sailboat on his way to visit his father. Both are in the story. Sources disagree on the distance: the 1898 record says 10 miles to the northward; LighthouseFriends says 12.5 statute miles; Rowlett gives 6 miles (10 km) off Thoney Point. The story keeps the sources' statute miles and does not convert to nautical miles. Tower height: 34 ft (USLHS) against 40 ft (Rowlett, LighthouseFriends). Sources disagree on when the historic light stopped: Rowlett says inactive since 1939; LighthouseFriends describes signal changes in 1943. Rowlett's 1995 Coast Guard tower is still active and is probably what the record's Fl W 6s describes. LighthouseFriends dates the NRHP listing to 1969; NPGallery gives 1983; the story gives both. The 1914 Bulletin confirms the oil-vapour change; the 60-second red flash is LighthouseFriends alone (the 1899 Board list gives 90 seconds). Automation in 1937 and the 1943 change are from LighthouseFriends only. No shipwreck or rescue tied to the light turned up in the LSS or Board texts read; the 1898 Marquette station entry is the one rescue-type record. Newspaper searches (Chronicling America, Michigan papers 1868-1945) gave nothing usable. People: Grant Kirkendall's memories are printed by LighthouseFriends and the owners' site; he may be living, so the editor may prefer to cut the coal sentence. Scott Holman is named as the published sources name him, in his role as buyer. Wikipedia was consulted for leads only and is not cited. Access: the USLHS record says the site is not open to the public; Rowlett says the site is open and the tower closed; LighthouseFriends says the grounds are closed. The story uses the strictest reading.
